voyage.name: Katoghike
voyage.alt: Holy Mother of God Kathoghike Church, Սուրբ Աստվածածին Կաթողիկէ Եկեղեցի
voyage.address: corner of Sayat-Nova Ave. and Abovian St
voyage.content: A tiny structure constructed in typical Armenian style. Katoghike means "cathedral"; the reason for the incongruity is that the original 13th century church had a much larger basilica attached to it in the 17th century - but that addition was demolished in 1936. In 2015 a new and much larger separate church was built next to Kathoghike, the cream colored St. Anna church.

voyage.name: Katoghike Tsiranavor Church of Avan
voyage.alt: Ավանի Սուրբ Աստվածածին Կաթողիկե Եկեղեցի, Katoghike Tsiranavor church, later renamed Surp Hovhannes
voyage.content: This is the city's oldest surviving church, which was completed in the 6th century.

voyage.name: St Gregory the Illuminator Cathedral
voyage.content: Completed in 2001 to commemorate the 1700th anniversary of Armenia as a Christian nation. The holy relics of St Gregory the Armenian were given back to the Armenian Church by the Vatican in 2001 and placed in this cathedral. The building is a megalomaniacal exaggeration of traditional Armenian Church Architecture. As opposed to all other churches in Yerevan (and Armenia) the cathedral is full of light and does not ca

voyage.name: Saint Sarkis Cathedral
voyage.content: From the Victory Bridge (or alternatively the Brandy Factory building) there is a beautiful view on the church and surroundings (structures of different shades constructed in immediate proximity to the church during the Soviet years of forced secularisation). The church is always crowded. Usually there are also many young people as St Sargis (or St Sergius in Western churches) is the patron saint of young people and

voyage.name: St Astvatsatsin of Nork
voyage.alt: Holy Cross Church, Սուրբ Խաչ եկեղեցու
voyage.address: Nork-Marash (Նորք-Մարաշ) administrative district, near to Olimpos Educational Complex
voyage.content: This is the replica of a beautiful 18th-century St Holy Mother of God (Sb Astvatsatsin in Armenian) church destroyed during the Soviet years of forced secularisation. Because of the sudden death of the benefactor the church complex was never finished.

voyage.name: St John The Baptist Church
voyage.content: A church with three naves, built in 1710 and renovated and expanded in the 1980s.

voyage.name: Erebuni Fortress
voyage.content: The excavations, recreations and museum of the nearly 3,000-year-old fortress that established Yerevan. Fairly well- (and maybe the best-) preserved fortress of Urartian Period in Armenia.

voyage.name: Republic Square
voyage.alt: Armenian: Հանրապետության Հրապարակ Russian: Площадь Республики
voyage.content: The city's main square is a grand example of Soviet public architecture. The early buildings (the Houses of Government, the Ministry of Communications and the Marriott Hotel) are Neo-Classical with Armenian hints. The later buildings (the Foreign Ministry and Art Gallery) are Modernist imitations.Within the square, the Singing Fountains perform most evenings April-Oct, dancing and frothing to classical and contempora

voyage.name: Northern Avenue
voyage.content: Impossible to miss, this pedestrian avenue was opened in 2008 connecting Opera with Republic Square, the two hubs of central Yerevan. It's a post-modern response to post-World War II Soviet Yerevan architecture. It is emerging as the shopping district, together with Sayat-Nova ave., Terian st., Tumanian st. and Abovian st.

voyage.name: Abovian street
voyage.content: It's home to very few remaining Belle Époque period structures of Republican Armenia. Some gems of Art Nouveau, early Modern (constructivist and the like), and Moorish Revival style can be found in the backyards of Abovian, Nalbandian and Hanrapetutian streets. Most often they are in a very poor condition due to neglect. Hanrapetutian st. might get a special attention if you are not time constrained.

voyage.name: Freedom (or Theatrical) Square
voyage.content: On the north the square is bordered by the Opera House, followed by a park with a lake and full of open air cafés on the east, and from south it borders the Northern Avenue

voyage.name: Mashtots avenue
voyage.content: It's the 8-lane highway of the city which somehow also accommodates a pedestrian zones on the sides (result of standard Soviet planning of main 'Prospekts'). It is overly noisy because of the heavy traffic (mostly unorganised public transportation) but the parts close to The Opera is a favourite hangout place for the locals. There are three buildings on the avenue which are well worth attention - Matenadaran, the cov

voyage.name: Matenadaran
voyage.content: Houses the world's largest collection of Armenian illuminated manuscripts, and one of the largest such collections of any kind in the world. A display room has a sampling of some of the finest works, and the additional cost of the guided tour is worthwhile. The building is dug into the hill and can withstand a nuclear attack. The white stone statue in front is of Mesrop Mashtots, teaching the Armenian alphabet, his i

voyage.name: Blue Mosque
voyage.content: An 18th-century Shia Islamic Mosque, one of the few surviving structures of a once (before Soviet secularisation) prospering Muslim community of Yerevan.

voyage.name: Cascades, Sculpture Park and Cafesjian Museum
voyage.content: The Sculpture Park is a small green zone in the immediate North of the Opera. Sculptures from Botero and other artists of international fame decorate the park. The park is part of Cafesjian Museum - the Armenian version of Guggenheim. The main part of the museum is in the Cascades - an Art Deco version of the Hanging Gardens of Babylon stretching nearly the height of the Empire State Building. It's a massive white st

voyage.name: Train Station and Sasuntsi David Statue
voyage.alt: Kayaran or David of Sassoun Square
voyage.content: Beautiful square and train station with Soviet classical architecture, and one of Armenia's most famous monuments - the soaring statue of Sasuntsi David (David of Sasun), which is often used as a symbol of the city.

voyage.name: Cascade Memorial to the Victims of Soviet Repression
voyage.content: Monument dedicated to the memory of the victims of Soviet-era murders and deportations, atop the Yerevan Cascade, next to the obelisk that commemorates 50 years of Soviet Armenia. The Cascade Memorial was designed by Jim Torosyan, Yerevan's chief architect between 1971 and 1981, and was constructed in the late 1980s and completed around 2008. Inside the large concrete structure, a memorial slab has the inscription of

voyage.name: Aram Khachaturyan House Museum
voyage.content: The home of late composer Aram Khachaturyan (1903-1978) has been turned into a museum. Things like his manuscripts and piano are on display here, and the building also has a concert hall.

voyage.name: The National Art Gallery
voyage.content: Founded in 1921, the Gallery preserves more than 42,000 works of Armenian and international fine art and decorative-applied arts. Its collections include masterpieces by world-renowned artists such as Hovhannes Aivazovsky, Vardges Sureniants, Arshile Gorky, Marc Chagall, Wassily Kandinsky, Donatello, Tintoretto, and many others. The Gallery also preservs unique fragments of medieval Armenian church frescoes from Arme

voyage.name: History Museum of Armenia
voyage.content: A roundup of the nation's history from early settlements to the 20th century. Lots of archaeological exhibits and pieces of art give an impression of each period. If you would like to move along the timeline then start at the top of the building. The early periods are amply annotated, but the English (and Russian) tags thin out considerably by mid-19th century, reappear in the exhibit dedicated to the Great Catastrop

voyage.name: Cafesjian Museum of Modern Art
voyage.hours: Escalators gallery daily 08:00-20:00; special galleries Fri-Sun 10:00-20:00
voyage.content: A modern art museum, housing the collection of Gerard Cafesjian. It has Arshile Gorky, Andy Warhol, Marc Chagall and other big names on display. The collection is very rich in Glass Art, has many pieces of the Libenský-Brychtová couple, including specially made 'For Armenia' series. Special galleries display monumental tryptichons or reliefs focusing on Armenian history. Entry can be made at any level, but informatio

voyage.name: The Yerevan History Museum
voyage.price: 400 dram. Tour in Russian, English, French, German 3,000 dram
voyage.content: Presents all periods of the life in Yerevan starting from paleolithic settlements (50,000 years) to modern days. Ancient maps and the pictures of the lost city, pre-Soviet Erivan, are of special interest. Lift and sloping floors for people who use wheelchairs.

voyage.name: Modern Art Museum of Yerevan
voyage.content: Houses quite a selection of contemporary art by mostly Armenian artists. On the opposite side of the street, there is the newly opened HayArt cultural center as well as the Eduard Isabekyan Gallery.

voyage.name: Erebuni Museum of History
voyage.price: 1,000 dram for museum and site; 500 dram for site only. Tour in foreign language 2,500 dram
voyage.content: The museum stands at the foot of the Arin Berd hill, on top of which the Urartian Fortress Erebouni has stood since 782 BCE. The City-Fortress was excavated, some parts of the structure were reinforced and restored, and the fortress was turned into an outdoor museum. The city was built by Argishti I the King of Urartu in 782 BCE. The temple of God Khaldi occupied an important place in the fortress. The walls of the t

voyage.name: Parajanov Museum
voyage.content: The House-Museum of Sergei Parajanov, a famous Soviet film director. The museum is best known for special Parajanov collages and art that everybody loves and enjoys. It is equally highly appreciated by children, teenagers and the most demanding art critics. Many highest level official informal meetings are conducted here. It is a must-see!

voyage.name: Martiros Saryan House-Museum
voyage.price: 1,000 dram. Tour in Russian, English, French 2,500 dram
voyage.content: If you are a lover of bright colours and enjoy Impressionist art then the House Museum of Martiros Saryan is a place for you. It's a 3-floor structure, designed by the artist and built during his lifetime, both as his home and a house for his heritage after his death.

voyage.name: Armenian Genocide Memorial (Genocide Museum & Tsitsernakaberd Monument)
voyage.content: An austere monument & museum commemorating the victims of the Armenian Genocide. The permanent collection documents the 19th C community, then its ruthless destruction circa 1915 at the hands of the Ottoman Empire.Tsitsernakaberd (meaning "Fortress of Swallows") is probably best reached by taxi. Walking from town, follow Athens St past the Hrazdan Stadium to Brazil Square roundabout, where a little lane branches nort

voyage.name: Museum of Woodwork
voyage.content: Houses some artifacts of Armenian historical wood carving culture (doors, furniture and the like), and wood-based sculptures by modern day artists.

voyage.name: Hovhannes Tumanyan Museum
voyage.content: Dedicated to renowned prominent thinker, writer, poet, fabulist and humanist Hovhannes Toumanian, with 18,000 exhibited items. Rooms of the Apartment are: Study Room, Guest Room, Dining Room, Children’s Room, Nvard Toumanian’s Room, Balcony, Olga’s Room,

voyage.name: Armenian Railways Museum
voyage.alt: Museum of Railway Transport of Armenia
voyage.address: Yerevan Railway Station, Armenia, 0005, Yerevan Sasuntsi Davti Sq.
voyage.content: Presents the history of the Armenian railway, from 1895. Exhibits are labelled in Armenian and Russian, but not English. Several large exhibits are in an adjacent garden, accessible from the museum. A steam locomotive and carriage stand in the station, and are accessed by crossing the tracks at the Yerevan end of the platforms.

voyage.name: Eduard Isabekyan Gallery
voyage.content: Small but good art museum, commemorating the eponymous artist. Housed in an interesting round building in Brutalist style.

voyage.name: Ervand Kochar Museum
voyage.content: Small museum dedicated to the eponymous sculptor and artist.

voyage.name: Soviet Club
voyage.content: Combination museum and restaurant with numerous Soviet-era household exhibits - cars, appliances, arcade games, and posters. Visitors can actually play the arcade games, dance to 1970s/1980s music, and enjoy food and drink from the era.

voyage.name: Fountain of David of Sasun
voyage.content: Built in 1948, around 460 m².

voyage.name: Fountains of Saryan Post Park
voyage.content: Tons of fountains - including a huge splash pad that kids love to run through in the summer.

voyage.name: 2,750 fountains of Shahumyan Park
voyage.content: When Yerevan celebrated its 2,750th birthday, this park opened a water feature with a fountain for each year of Yerevan's history.

voyage.name: Singing Fountains
voyage.content: The big fountains of Republic Square with a music, light and of course dancing water show every evening.

voyage.name: Sunken Fountain
voyage.content: At the foot of the Cascade complex, which itself has many fountains, this sunken fountain with lots of seating is one of Yerevan's coolest spots to escape the heat of summer.

voyage.name: The Ararat Cognac Factory
voyage.alt: Ararat Wine Brandy Vodka Factory Museum
voyage.content: The oldest factory in Armenia. Offers tours and tasting, but the people there are very uptight and the place is overrun by tourists.

voyage.name: Levon's Divine Underground
voyage.content: Levon Arakelyan's wife asked him to dig a potato storage cellar, but instead of this he created a complex structure of stairs, corridors and rooms inside a rock. It took him 23 years to do this until he died in 2007. His wife now organises excursions showing these undergrounds.

voyage.name: Mother Armenia
voyage.content: Erected in 1967, replacing the monumental statue of Joseph Stalin.

voyage.name: National Assembly of Armenia
voyage.content: Yellow brick building, finished in 1950 to house the Supreme Soviet of Armenia. Today it serves as the parliament building.

voyage.name: Yerevan City Hall
voyage.content: The city's administration is housed in this massive five-story building. Construction started during Soviet times, was halted in 1991 for over a decade and the building was finally completed in 2004. The Yerevan History Museum is attached to it.

voyage.name: Walk of Fame
voyage.content: Stars, embedded in the pavement, commemorating twelve Armenian actors and musicians.

voyage.name: Hrazdan Gorge partying
voyage.content: Visit one of the themed restaurants in the Hrazdan Gorge to see the locals partying. The food does not tend to venture far from barbecue and crayfish, but it is usually good barbecue, and the prices range from very reasonable to the unreasonable. Check the prices on the hard liquor and wines before ordering a bottle if you’re price sensitive.

voyage.name: Climb the Cascades
voyage.content: (or - before 20:00 - take the escalators inside the art gallery, stepping outside at each level) one evening for the great views of the city and Mt. Ararat, then head across the street to the amusement park inside Victory Park for some cotton candy and a ride on the rickety Ferris wheel.

voyage.name: Catch a concert
voyage.content: on the Cascades or the Lover's Park, and an art exhibition at Swan Lake park or Lover's Park.

voyage.name: Yerevan Water World
voyage.hours: 12:00–21:00, indoor water park "Aquatek" is open all year round without holidays
voyage.content: A water park popular with the locals in the summers, it consists of a big open-air water park and a much smaller indoor one. Anybody can cool down there as in total it offers 7 outdoor and 3 indoor pools. There are also wall-climbing facilities. During winter time, the largest pool of the park is turned into an ice skating rink.

voyage.name: Yerevan Zoo
voyage.price: Adult 800 dram, children 12-16 years - 500 dram, children 3-12 years - 300 dram
voyage.content: Zoo is home to about 3,000 animals mainly representing South Caucasus and Armenia: bears, goats, snakes, Armenian mouflon and black vultures. Also from other parts of the world: lions, tigers, hyenas and an Asian elephants. It was upgraded and renovated to the modern standards back in 2014.

voyage.name: Spartak Stadium
voyage.content: This is a mixed-use sports & athletics stadium just south of city centre.

voyage.name: Botanical garden of Yerevan
voyage.content: The collection includes more than 200 species of endemic, rare and declining plants. However, after the collapse of the Soviet Union due to insufficient funds the condition of the park started declining and now it needs a lot of improvements.

voyage.name: Children's Railway Park
voyage.content: Miniature railway for children to ride in, established in 1937.

voyage.name: Children's Park
voyage.content: Yet another beautiful remnant of Soviet urban planning in Yerevan. The park, opened in 1937, is situated in a gorgeous canyon of Hrazdan river and features a children's railway. Though the park and the railway still function, most of the infrastructure is horribly deteriorated. On the other hand the deterioration gives the feeling of a 'ghost park from a fairy tale' even though it is always populated. From Missak Man

voyage.name: Circular park
voyage.content: Despite its name, the park's shape is semi-circular. You can see several monuments to important Armenian and Russian imperial figures here.

voyage.name: English park
voyage.content: One of Yerevan's oldest parks, though smaller in size than it once was. It is popular with couples for wedding photographs.

voyage.name: Park of Komitas Pantheon
voyage.content: A cemetery that doubles as a park.

voyage.name: Lover's Park
voyage.content: One of the oldest parks of Yerevan. Renovated in tradition of Japanese landscaping with Armenian spirit. It often hosts open air art exhibitions and concerts. It is best reached by metro, station 'Marshal Baghramian' - perhaps the most underused building and allegedly the best in Modernist style.

voyage.name: Lyon Park
voyage.content: Surrounding the artificial Vardarvar Lake, this park was renamed Lyon Park to honor France's second city. Lyon is a friendship city of Yerevan and the French funded the renovation of the park in the early 2010s.

voyage.name: Oghakadzev park
voyage.content: Features the Luna Park amusement park, a couple of small lakes and cafés.

voyage.name: Opera park
voyage.content: Spend a late night at a café in the Opera park, and outside the Melody Café for some of the best people watching in Yerevan.

voyage.name: Paplavok Park
voyage.content: Chill out in Yerevan Green Belt.

voyage.name: Saryan Park
voyage.content: A triangular park with a statue of the painter Martiros Saryan is where painters gather to sell their work. Many more on the weekend than on weekdays.

voyage.name: The Swan Lake park
voyage.content: ends with the popular statue of the composer Arno Babajanyan, which brings attention to his famous nose and long fingers. The Swan Lake park usually hosts various open air art exhibitions. Ice-skate with many locals at the Swan Lake (next to the Opera House) during winter months.

voyage.name: Tumanyan park
voyage.content: Part of the Tumo Centre for Creative Technologies.

voyage.name: Yerevan reservoir
voyage.content: Built in 1963, total area is 57.45 ha.

voyage.name: Victory Park
voyage.content: - Amusement park. Features a huge monument of Mother Armenia as well as some Soviet military equipment on display. Very nice view of the city centre.

voyage.name: The Opera House
voyage.content: The building is perhaps modeled after SemperOper of Dresden, however it is supposed to be double as beautiful as the Yerevan building is two sided: One side (entrance from the Theatrical/Freedom square) is home to Opera and Ballet Theatre, while the street side houses the Khachaturian Concert Hall. For music fans, attend cheap and excellent performances at the Opera or the Chamber Music Orchestra. If a national dance

voyage.name: Moscow theatre
voyage.content: Opened in 1936, with 4 theatre halls.

voyage.name: Sundukyan State Academic Theatre
voyage.content: The oldest modern theatre in Armenia, here you can see the most famous actors of the country perform.

voyage.name: Arten Theatre
voyage.content: Independent chamber theatre founded in 2022, in a former House of Culture with about 50 seats. Performances, play readings, labs and lectures; the programme is on the website.

voyage.name: Yerevan Circus
voyage.content: A new circus building finished in 2018, on the place of a former one which was demolished in 2012. Opening of the circus was planned for 2020, postponed by the pandemic and as of 2024 it has still yet to open.

voyage.name: Yerevan's Birthday
voyage.content: Yerevan's birthday is usually celebrated on the second Saturday of October. It's usually a huge event, with central Yerevan being pedestrian only: there are many stages all over the city for theatrical or music (usually thematic - ethnic minorities, folk, jazz, rock, pop and classics) performances with a culmination on Republic Square. The festival is centered around the Erebuni fortress, since it is the cradle of Ye

voyage.name: Golden Apricot
voyage.content: A fairly well-established international film festival, usually held in July. Armenians take pride in it.

voyage.name: ReAnimania
voyage.content: An emerging international animated film festival held in autumn.

voyage.name: Covered Market
voyage.alt: Agricultural bazaar, G.U.M. market, Food Market No. 2
voyage.content: Yerevan's largest food market.

voyage.name: Vernissage
voyage.content: A walk through the weekend Vernissage open air market through the park between Aram and Buzand Streets is a must. From rugs, souvenirs, instruments and paintings, to pets and chemistry supplies, this outdoor market seemingly has everything.

voyage.name: Dalma Garden Mall
voyage.content: Western-style indoor mall with food court and movie theater.

voyage.name: Yerevan Mall
voyage.content: Western-style indoor mall with food court, movie theater and play area. Anchored by Carrefour.

voyage.name: Metronome Shopping Centre
voyage.content: Pretty small underground mall in the center.

voyage.name: RIO Mall
voyage.content: Newer mall in the Arabkir/Komitas neighborhood.

voyage.name: General Market
voyage.content: A supermarket.

voyage.name: SAS supermarket
voyage.content: A chain. More units: 35 Isahakyan St (16px: Yeritasardakan), 18 Mashtots (16px: Hanrapetutian Hraparak (Republic Square)), 31 Tumanyan (close to Armenian Opera Theater), 85 Baghramyan (16px: Barekamutyun), 20/1 Qajaznuni, 1A Kievyan

voyage.name: Master Class
voyage.content: Angus beef kebab sandwiches for 1500 drams (Oct 2026), and a few other items on the small, focused menu.

voyage.name: Mer Taghe
voyage.content: A small lahmejun joint on Tumanyan, and their lahmejuns have a big following. If you have some extra time and want to splurge, try the manti dumplings or the norahars, a kind of regional lasagna.

voyage.name: OST
voyage.content: Cheap cafe, lots of food options and drinks. Very central, try the Ajarakan khachapuri or the lahmejun. Free Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Meghedi
voyage.content: Cheap cafe, lots of food options and drinks. Very central, next to the Opera at the Freedom Square. Free Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Tumanyan Shaurma
voyage.content: Yerevan style shawarma. A local chain with a dozen restaurants around Yerevan.

voyage.name: Artashi Mot
voyage.content: Cheap shaurmas, soups and kebabs upstairs, fancier but still well priced sit-down restaurant underground. Great place to have BBQ and to meet your traditional fast food cravings. The fancier part is considered by many to be the finest place for khorovats (BBQ) in Armenia. Judge for yourself, but not before trying the horti (beef) and sunki (mushroom) barbeques. They are both delicious, when they have them. Other nice

voyage.name: Jengyalov Hac
voyage.content: Bakery. Excellent Armenian zhangyalov hats.

voyage.name: Lahmajun Gaidz
voyage.content: Good cheap Armenian fast food, run by a kind and hard working Syrian-Armenian woman.

voyage.name: Tun Lahmajo
voyage.content: uper affordable lahmajo (Armenian pizza) and always packed with locals

voyage.name: Grand Candy Ponchikanots
voyage.content: Ponchiks are a regional type of donut. Fried dough stuffed with a custard and topped with powdered sugar. Grand Candy took over the old space of a popular former Soviet "ponchikanots", or place of ponchiks and this is a popular spot for a fresh, hot, and very cheap treat. Lots of locally made candy and chocolate for sale as well. Grand Candy's big competition in the ponchik realm came down from Gyumri and opened up a

voyage.name: Tumanyan Khinkali
voyage.content: Khinkali (sturdy soup dumplings, similar to xiao long bao that came to Caucasus over the Silk Road) with meat or cheese filling is the name of the game here. You can have them boiled or fried; they are priced per dumpling, and 6-8 should be enough for an average appetite. If you try using knife and fork, you'll end up with a pool of soup on your plate; grab the dumpling by the bunched top, bite out a notch in the sid

voyage.name: Anteb
voyage.content: A family-run cafe that serves a huge variety of kebabs in a very casual cafe-type setting. The Adana and Urfa are a bargain at about 800 dram each and the Iskender, though slightly more expensive for 3,000 dram (May 2015) rivals the best. The rice pudding is pricey but tasty. Cheap drinks and free fresh hot pocket bread.

voyage.name: Caucasus Tavern
voyage.content: Extensive menu of Caucasian dishes in 5 languages plus photos. You can order fish straight from the aquarium.

voyage.name: Old Erivan
voyage.content: Offers traditional food, songs, dances and the décor will make you think Disney has come to town. Almost a must for any visitor.

voyage.name: Tavern Yerevan
voyage.content: The place for traditional Armenian cuisine. You'll have to rub shoulders with an occasional government function, a wedding shower or a busful of tourists, but the food is the real thing. Do not be scared by the names of the dishes - the more unpronounceable, the tastier (tzhvzhik, for example, is fegata alla veneziana, offal with fried onions - delicious!), and the English menu has helpful descriptions and pictures.

voyage.name: Twelve Tables
voyage.content: Very cozy spot with 12 tables, smoke-free, good menu with nice salads, soups, comfort food, and great desserts and teas. Non-smoking.

voyage.name: Lavash
voyage.content: Very good menu of traditional Armenian cuisine. The large room upstairs is a more refined white-tablecloth experience, but prices are the same. Can be busy on weekend nights, reserve ahead. Absolutely end the meal with the famous millefeuille cake (layers of fillo and pastry custard); trying to save some space for it is a lost cause, however - the one-serving slab is enormous even for two (and sometimes they will bri

voyage.name: Ktoor
voyage.content: Typical Armenian menu, done very well, reasonably priced, with a very large outdoor patio in front on the far end of Saryan Street. They have some ridiculously large dishes that are perfect for large groups.

voyage.name: The Coast
voyage.content: Great international food menu at Cascade. Good breakfast, lunch and dinner options.

voyage.name: Gata Tavern
voyage.content: Hearty portions, feels like a homestyle kitchen.

voyage.name: Gini Pig
voyage.content: Wine, beer and pizza in a small, rustic space, run by an Australian-Armenian fellow. A favorite of many for the food and vibe.

voyage.name: Dolmama
voyage.content: Fusion Armenian-World cuisine. Excellent food, service and ambience. The outdoor seating out back is a way to experience the old courtyards that filled central Yerevan in the past.

voyage.name: The Club
voyage.price: For a budget option, you can order one of their very filling thin crust pizzas, starting at US$5
voyage.content: Has some excellent Western Armenian dishes, including manti, su borek and the amazing midia dolma. The underground space is very hip, and the tea room, when not too smoky is a good place to sit on a bean bag and chat.

voyage.name: Voskevaz
voyage.content: Good menu of meats, salads, starters, and wine.

voyage.name: Limone
voyage.content: Great Napolitano pizzas, nice salads and sandwiches, fancy drinks and desserts, located right by Cascade.

voyage.name: Asador
voyage.content: Surf and turf. Steaks from around the world, and fresh seafood flown in. Excellent wine selection as well.

voyage.name: Calumet
voyage.content: Bohemian, friendly, alternative crowd. Insanely smokey (seriously). There is no outdoor section so if you're not a fan of cigarette smoke, it might not be the place for you. English speaking staff and solid drinks selection. A nice place to kill a night.

voyage.name: Roza
voyage.content: Small bar with great ambiance in old Yerevan building, and fantastic drinks. Try the Tutovni house cocktail made with the famous local mulberry vodka.

voyage.name: In Vino
voyage.content: The first wine bar on Saryan Street, that led the transformation of the entire neighborhood is still popular.

voyage.name: Jack's Pub
voyage.content: Good spot for a drink, the bloody mary is legendary and the basil gin cocktail is great in the summer. You'll likely meet some repats here.

voyage.name: Mirzoyan Library
voyage.content: Started out as a space in a traditional courtyard with a collection of photography books, it's now a café with very nice drinks and creative and excellent bites and sweets. Free wifi.

voyage.name: Kami Club
voyage.content: Live music on many nights.

voyage.name: Stop Club
voyage.content: Rock club. Live music on many nights.

voyage.name: Balcony Villa Hostel
voyage.price: 9,000 dram for single room, 6,000 dram for shared room with locker, 6,500 dram for room with light breakfast, 7,000 dram for full breakfast. Between November and May rooms are 5,000 dram.
voyage.content: A small, budget hostel. Offers free wifi, laundry, a kitchen and shared bathrooms that are cleaned daily. English speaking, friendly, coffee and tea are free.

voyage.name: Envoy Hostel
voyage.content: Winner of 'Best Hostel in Armenia' Award by HW 2010&11&13. Is centrally located, large and comfortable with free internet/wifi access, breakfast and tea/coffee facilities. All the rooms and common areas are air conditioned and spotlessly clean. English speaking staff is efficient and knowledgeable about traveling in Armenia and the regions. They also have a hostel in Tbilisi and offer weekly tours from Yerevan to Tbi

voyage.name: Grammy Hostel
voyage.content: A hostel, with a travellers' desk, free internet access, breakfast just for extra 500 dram, laundry, TV, a relaxation room where you can chill out and escape from the Yerevan hustle and bustle of the city, and a little garden where you can soak up the sun and relax on a bench.

voyage.name: Hostel Glide
voyage.price: Prices for beds start from 4,500 dram
voyage.content: A private house located two metro stops out of the centre, but in a quiet and safe place. It's very close to bus stations, and it is possible to see Ararat mountain from the windows. Run by a very hospitable family.

voyage.name: Theatre Hostel
voyage.price: The prices start from 4,500 dram with light breakfast included
voyage.content: A small and cozy hostel 5 minutes walking distance from the main square. It is very clean, has many free facilities, such as Wi-Fi internet access, bicycle parking zone, etc.

voyage.name: Yerevan Hostel
voyage.content: In the centre, 3 minutes from the 16px: Republic Square. Friendly, knowledgeable English speaking staff available 24 hours a day. Very clean hostel, showers with hot water available day and night. Wifi available also a computer available for guests. Traditional breakfast prepared upon request, so always fresh. Flexible check in/check out times. Bag storage.

voyage.name: Bass Boutique Hotel
voyage.content: Small affordable 4-star.

voyage.name: Hotel Europe
voyage.content: Nice little central 3-star hotel.

voyage.name: Erebuni Hotel
voyage.content: 3 star, good value for price, comfort and location.

voyage.name: Mia Casa Hotel
voyage.content: Small 3-star.

voyage.name: Hotel Olympia
voyage.content: 2 km northwest of centre but compensated by great views over river gorge towards Aragats.

voyage.name: Royal Palace Hotel
voyage.content: Small hotel, in a quiet area of the city.

voyage.name: ibis Yerevan Center
voyage.content: Very central nice new hotel with very flexible pricing depending, but generally mid-range prices or lower.

voyage.name: Ararat Hotel
voyage.content: Four star going on 2 or 3, many negative reviews.

voyage.name: Armenia Marriott Hotel
voyage.content: International hotel with fine rooms and facilities, great location.

voyage.name: Best Western Congress Hotel
voyage.content: The Congress is one step down in price but offers the same western feel as the Marriott, and has a large outdoor pool.

voyage.name: Golden Palace Hotel
voyage.content: Pleasant central 5 star hotel.

voyage.name: Grand Hotel Yerevan
voyage.content: 5 star hotel with old charm and modern amenities: roof top pool, elegant guest rooms, restaurant, conference halls, winter garden with 24-hr bar and other services.

voyage.name: Tufenkian Historic Yerevan Hotel
voyage.content: 4 star hotel with restaurant near to Vernissage market.

voyage.name: Ani Plaza
voyage.content: Boxy 4-star, good accommodation for the price.

voyage.name: Hotel Latar
voyage.content: Way out on edge of city, you'll need a car. The massive circular pool is a sight to behold.
